slot.brief: Figure shows an unsymmetrical ether; ask which alcohol/alkyl iodide forms when cleaved by excess hot HI, and why the cleavage site is chosen.

verdicts.working: HI protonates the ether; cleavage at the tertiary carbon gives tert-butyl iodide and methanol. Excess hot HI converts methanol to methyl iodide, so both carbon-containing products are iodides.

working:
The compound is methyl tert-butyl ether, (CH3)3C-O-CH3. With hot HI, protonated ether cleavage occurs by SN1 at the tertiary centre because the (CH3)3C+ carbocation is stable. This forms tert-butyl iodide and methanol. Excess HI then converts methanol to methyl iodide, CH3OH + HI to CH3I + H2O. Final products are tert-butyl iodide and methyl iodide.

Independent check: HI protonates the ether; cleavage at the tertiary carbon gives tert-butyl iodide and methanol. Excess hot HI converts methanol to methyl iodide, so both carbon-containing products are iodides.
solution:
HI protonates the ether; cleavage occurs at the tertiary carbon by the $S_N1$ pathway, forming tert-butyl iodide and methanol.
$$\mathrm{(CH_3)_3C-O-CH_3 + HI \rightarrow (CH_3)_3C-I + CH_3OH}$$
With excess hot HI, $\mathrm{CH_3OH + HI \rightarrow CH_3I + H_2O}$; hence the products are tert-butyl iodide and methyl iodide.
